name: Qualitative Methods Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for qualitative methods work: a short set of checks to run before calling a qualitative methods task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for qualitative methods work: a short set of checks to run before calling a qualitative methods task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When qualitative methods guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Before starting qualitative methods work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
3. When multiple qualitative methods strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. When qualitative methods decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. Validate qualitative methods outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. Keep qualitative methods changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. Document any non-obvious qualitative methods decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Prefer explicit, readable qualitative methods solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting qualitative methods assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of qualitative methods correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated qualitative methods concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new qualitative methods abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for qualitative methods, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
